Since this was before Perry Mason, it is an invalid argument to say that he's just playing Perry Mason. Besides that, he's got a libido in this film, which Perry didn't have much of. You can also see this movie on your Roku player (Moonlight Movies). Excellent forgotten film.

Both Burr & Lansbury were superb in a great noir film. It is easy to see this film influence Burr's casting as Perry Mason shortly afterwards and Lansbury;s darkness foreshadowed her role The Manchurian Candidate.

This is a very enjoyable story of love and intrigue, with a fascinating twist at the end. A real potboiler, although the sound at some points was not quite as clear as would be desired; even so, this film is definitely worth watching, and Lansbury is quite beautiful in her role.

If all this wasn't enough, add a solid cast that consists of Lionel Atwill, Fay Wray and Melvin Douglas. This is a vampire movie, but not the kind you think. Discovering what sort of evil ghoul is at work is half the fun in watching this atmospheric little thriller. A minor distraction is the overuse of comic relief supplied by Maude Eburne. Nevertheless "The Vampire Bat" is a horror quickie that honestly earns its four stars.
A fun way to pass an hour.
It has Dwight Frye, Lionel Atwill, and Fay Wray, so you can't miss. Don't expect high production values. This is a B-film, but a good little creepy one with fun performances.

I give it 4 stars just because Ms Wray is in it.....also good entertainment for any stormy night gathered around the fireplace or whatever.

ArchiveUser15149 has helped to save for the ages this wonderful gem, The Vampire Bat. I can't imagine anyone that wouldn't enjoy this movie & would feel confident in perhaps even saying that it was family friendly.

A good cast lurks through this stiff spookfest, which features good sets, a sometimes intelligent script, and some agonizing attempts at comic relief. Faye is beautiful and Douglas rises above the material.

A fascinating historical document which outlines Japan just before the outbreak of World War II. Just looking at the year of the film (1941) makes you wonder how much time passed before this film was made and when Japan struck Pearl Harbor. Anyways, the film is a bout 2 children and their family and all their cute Japanese customs. The film is a bit racist and stereotypically Japanese, but that can be excused for the time period. A interesting film to watch, and it is recommended.

Well-shot scenes highlight this 1940 film, which consists of a day in the life of two Japanese school children. It shows customs of the era just before their elders launched a sneak attack on Pearl Harbor. The kids get to eat tofu and sea-foam candy. And they bathe once a day, too. The film includes looped dialogue (sometimes when mouths are closed) and sound effects, along with James Brill's droning narration.

Given the date of this film, this is a surprisingly kind treatment of the Japanese people, focusing on a well-off family and their daily activities. I assume the principal audience for this film was American school children. I rather doubt it was shown after December 7, 1941.

jsc2017m000730_NASA-Cribs-Human-Explorat: Follow along as interns at NASA’s Johnson Space Center show you around the Human Exploration Research Analog (HERA), a mission simulation environment located onsite at the Johnson Space Center in Houston. HERA is a unique three-story habitat designed to serve as an analog for isolation, confinement, and remote conditions in exploration scenarios. This video gives a tour of where crew members live, work, sleep, and eat during the analog missions.
MaxLaunchAbortSystemTest: NASA has successfully demonstrated an alternate system for future astronauts to escape their launch vehicle. The unpiloted launch tested an alternate concept for safely propelling a future spacecraft and its crew away from a problem on the launch pad or during ascent. iBPVKPb1BllBNDb7XKumV7soJlf9y6: “Understanding Electronics: Vacuum Tubes” is a color, educational film from 1970. Presented by Universal Education and Visual Arts in collaboration with educators from both the Toronto and Scarborough Boards of Education, this film educates its audience on the history, makes and models, and applications of vacuum tubes/ electron tubes. The vacuum tube is a device that controls electric current flow in a high vacuum between electrodes to which an electric potential difference has been applied.
